content.text: MLE is great, but it is not the only way to estimate parameters! This section introduces an alternate algorithm, Maximum A Posteriori (MAP). The paradigm of MAP is that we should choose the value for our parameters that is the most likely given the data. At first blush this might seem the same as MLE, however notice that MLE chooses the value of parameters that makes the

Parameter Priors

In order to get ready for the world of MAP estimation, we are going to need to brush up on our distributions. We will need reasonable distributions for each of our different parameters. A desideratum for prior distributions is that the resulting posterior distribution has the same functional form. We call these "conjugate" priors. In the case where you are updating your belief many times, conjugate priors makes programming in the math equations much easier.
